# Mathematical and Physical Reference {.unnumbered}

This appendix compiles the core physical equations, timing bounds, and coordinate transformation laws used throughout the manual.


## Dynamic Stopping Bounds

The dynamic stopping distance $d_{\text{stop}}$ represents the minimum clearance required to bring a moving physical actuator to rest before colliding with an obstacle:

$$d_{\text{stop}}(t) = v(t) \cdot t_{\text{delay}}(t) + \frac{v(t)^2}{2 \cdot a_{\text{max}}}$$

Where total delay $t_{\text{delay}}$ includes all latency tails and transport latencies:

$$t_{\text{delay}}(t) = t_{\text{transduce}} + \Delta t_{\text{age}}(t) + t_{\text{comm}} + t_{\text{enforce}} + t_{\text{actuator\_response}}$$

* **Current Velocity ($v(t)$):** Instantaneous physical velocity ($\text{m/s}$).
* **Maximum Safe Deceleration ($a_{\text{max}}$):** Maximum available braking deceleration ($\text{m/s}^2$).
* **Sensory Age ($\Delta t_{\text{age}}$):** Age of the sensory observation used to compute the decision ($\text{s}$).


## Spatial Frame Transformations

A rigid body transformation from source frame $A$ to target frame $B$ is represented by a homogeneous transformation matrix $T_B^A \in SE(3)$:

$$T_B^A = \begin{bmatrix} R_B^A & p_B^A \\ 0_{1\times 3} & 1 \end{bmatrix} \in \mathbb{R}^{4 \times 4}$$

Where $R_B^A \in SO(3)$ is the $3 \times 3$ rotation matrix and $p_B^A \in \mathbb{R}^3$ is the translation vector.

### Tangent Space Integration
To integrate velocities smoothly without gimbal lock singularities:

$$T(t + \Delta t) = T(t) \cdot \exp(\xi^\wedge \cdot \Delta t)$$

Where $\xi = [v, \omega]^T \in \mathbb{R}^6$ represents the linear and angular twist vector.


## Information Freshness Decay

Information freshness $\Delta t$ measures the time elapsed between physical event occurrence and actuation response:

$$\Delta t_{\text{total}} = (t_{\text{actuation}} - t_{\text{transduction}})$$

If target state changes at characteristic velocity $v_{\text{target}}$, spatial uncertainty expands as:

$$\sigma_{\text{pos}}(t) = \sigma_0 + v_{\text{target}} \cdot \Delta t_{\text{total}}$$


## Control Barrier Invariants

A safety envelope is defined by a continuously differentiable barrier function $h(x) \ge 0$:

$$\dot{h}(x, u) \ge -\gamma(h(x))$$

If $h(x) \ge 0$ defines the safe operational set, any proposed control vector $u$ is permitted only if it guarantees that $h(x)$ remains non-negative for all future time.
